hook: SCP-2952 is a corgi. A very, very long corgi, stretched across continents, and the article is every bit as charming as that sounds. It is mostly light and whimsical, though it borrows the sharp edge of old fairy tales, so a few of the retaliations are nastier than you might expect. Keep an eye on the footnotes, which carry some of the best jokes.
whyItMatters: It shows how the Foundation format can be bent toward pure delight without losing its procedural flavor. The piece pulls in fairy folklore, with offerings of milk and honey, polite apologies in Welsh and the danger of offending the small folk, and merges it with the mundane world of public transit. That collision of the mythic and the commuter-grade is the engine of the whole article.
thingsToNotice:
The dog is a subway line for three-centimetre fairies, and the Foundation's first move was to bury its stations. The riders answer like the fair folk of legend: the project director wakes up turned into a mole, seventeen construction workers find their walls swapped for poison ivy and deathcaps, and the researcher who tested the corgi's healing wakes with nightshade berries in his mouth and hawthorn stakes through his hands and feet, wounds that a footnote says were never undone.

Once the stations are reopened and the offerings start, the punchline arrives as a thank-you note from the Tylwyth Teg's transport director praising the Foundation's customer service and granting free rides on the C.O.R.G.I. system. The exploration log is then just an ordinary commute in miniature: a late train blamed on the dog's kidney stones, a petition about mice, a reeking mushroom snack. Agent Davies ends it by patting the corgi's side and calling him a good boy.

related.note: A picture resembling it shows up among the graffiti inside the fairy train car.
Named on a horror movie poster hanging in the same car.
